pictures.t: Tectonic sketch map of North-Eastern Sicily and Southern Calabria
pictures.c: Quaternary faults in North-Eastern Sicily and Southern Calabria with their Late Pleistocene uplift rate. CDOF: Capo d'Orlando Fault (Scicchitano et al., [2011])

pictures.t: Marine terraces between Capo d'Orlando and Acquedolci
pictures.c: Four orders of marine terraces located at elevations of 200 m, 120-90 m, 60-45 m, and 35-10 m a.s.l. between Capo d'Orlando and Acquedolci (Scicchitano et al., [2011])

pictures.t: Inner edges elevations in the Capo d'Orlando area with topographic profiles traces
pictures.c: Inner-edge elevations of paleoshorelines for the Capo d'Orlando area. Fifteen topographic profiles were producted perpendicular to the strike of the inferred fault, and their traces are shown in panel b (Meschis et al., [2018])

pictures.t: Quaternary paleoshorelines tilted and deformed by the inferred Capo D'Orlando Fault
pictures.c: Correlation of terraces along the strike of the inferred Capo d'Orlando Fault. Panel a shows an uplift rate of 0.35 mm/yr in the hangingwall, and of 0.89 mm/yr toward the inferred fault tip. Uplift varies along the strike of the inferred fault, with folded and tilted paleoshorelines (panel b). Higher terraces present higher tilt angle values (panel c; Meschis et al., [2018])
